description:
In partnership with the I.A.T.S.E. Local 52, Reel Works is hosting an intensive training program to prepare New Jerseyans with the essential skills needed to work successfully as on-set Grips and Electrics for the state’s growing film/tv industry.

Grip department is responsible for construction, rigging, and camera support for shooting and lighting.

Electric department is responsible for safely distributing temporary power systems, placing fixtures, and powering equipment across all production departments.

Training Eligibility Requirement:

  • Be at least 21+ years of age
  • Must be a NJ Resident within a 70-mile radius (1.5 hrs max) of Fort Monmouth
  • Have a desire to work in the TV and Film industry
  • A willingness to work long hours
  • Comfortable with heights (Recommended)

Grip Requirements

  • Have experience using hand and power tools


Electric Specific

  • Pass math exam
  • Familiarity with wiring/electrical equipment

There is no fee for this program. Participants are paid a stipend during the training.

Learn more at: mediamkrs.org/career-development

description:
Join us for

ACTIVE MINDS SPEAKER

Pablo Campos

Pablo Campos grew up angry and frustrated, not knowing why he had these feelings or how to express them positively. Despite a family history of depression, substance use disorder and anxiety, there was no discussion about mental health in his home. Lacking healthy coping skills, Pablo engaged in risk-taking behaviors including misuse of substances, eventually leading him to attempt to take his own life while still in high school. After multiple stays at in-patient facilities and finding proper treatment, Pablo began his road to recovery. He eventually gained further stability by adopting a strong work ethic, which began at the front desk of a health club. There he learned a great deal about having a healthy body and a healthy mind, and is a strong advocate for good nutrition, physical fitness and self-care. He now talks publicly about stigma and the lack of education around seeking help that delayed his recovery, and how building a strong network of professionals and loved ones has set him on a course for mental wellness.

Pablo served as a founding member and president of the Active Minds chapter at Pensacola State College and also worked at the Crisis Action Referral Effort for Students or CARES office at Pensacola State. After receiving his AA in Social Work from PSC he moved to Raleigh, NC where he earned his Bachelor and Master of Social Work degrees from North Carolina State University working towards attaining his LCSW.

Wednesday, September 30, 2026

12 p.m. - 1 p.m.

Journal Square Campus
Gabert Library
71 Sip Avenue
Sixth Floor, Atrium
Jersey City, NJ

description:
The Literary Lounge

SEPTEMBER PICK:

The Picture of Dorian Gray

by Oscar Wilde

 
Enthralled by his own exquisite portrait, Dorian Gray exchanges his soul for eternal youth and beauty. Influenced by his friend Lord Henry Wotton, he is drawn into a corrupt double life; indulging his desires in secret while remaining a gentleman in the eyes of polite society. Only his portrait bears the traces of his decadence. The novel was a succès de scandale and the book was later used as evidence against Wilde at the Old Bailey in 1895. It has lost none of its power to fascinate and disturb.



Our next meeting will take place on Tuesday, October 6 at 2 pm.

Open to all HCCC students, staff, faculty & community members.

HCCC’s always-anticipated Subscription Dining Series is fast approaching, and subscriptions for this in-demand fall fixture are expected to sell out quickly. Your involvement gives our culinary students the chance to perfect their craft and accumulate the hours needed to complete their required externships with you by their side. Location: Culinary Conference Center Time: 12:00 P.M. to 2:00 P.M. Dates: September 25, October 2, 9, 16, 23, 30, November 13, and 20 (HCCC is closed on Friday, November 6 for Diwali.) Subscriptions for the full series are $1,679 for all eight weeks*, or $899 for a half series subscription. Please note that half series subscriptions can only be the first four dates or the last four dates. *Single weeks are not available. Our menu consists of unique meals and service prepared entirely by our students: Appetizer, entree, dessert, non-alcoholic beverages, and other surprises! Seating is limited to four diners per table, per week. Gratuity not included. Payment can be sent to: HCCC Foundation 26 Journal Square, 14th Floor Jersey City, NJ 07306 Click here to pay online. Email us at name@example.org for more information or call 000-000-0000.
